selection_rule: Select a graphic by the evidence task for each story beat. Tactical diagrams are one option, never the default for every beat.

layouts.purpose: Explain a shape, run, press, or available space.
layouts.sourcing: The authored illustrative pitch is labeled as a diagram; match footage remains a separate approved asset.

layouts.purpose: Compare a small number of sourced team or player metrics.
Show where a claim or dataset came from and when it was published.
Compare numeric values with a paired, labeled horizontal bar display.
Show sourced values changing across ordered match moments or dates.

data_integrity: Only render values supplied by reviewed evidence.
Missing source or values means omit the numeric visualization and use a source-needed editorial card.
Show value labels and source attribution; color alone never encodes meaning.
No radar chart unless normalized comparable data and its benchmark are explicitly provided.
previews: Renderer-exported examples in previews/ are illustrative and use no real match or citation.

statline_scorecard.composition: Dark split scoreboard; two teams face inward across centered metric labels.
statline_scorecard.visual_encoding: Large paired values plus mirrored within-row strokes; labels and source remain explicit.
statline_scorecard.best_for: A compact head-to-head of comparable team/player metrics.

chart_comparison.composition: Warm chalk plotting sheet with an open chart area and visible vertical scale.
chart_comparison.visual_encoding: Zero-baseline bars, grid ticks, direct values and labels; no surrounding stat cards.
chart_comparison.best_for: Comparing one numeric measure across teams or categories.

chart_timeline.composition: Warm chalk plotting sheet with a chronological line and event points.
chart_timeline.visual_encoding: Ordered labels, visible values, line path and source note.
chart_timeline.best_for: Showing how a measure changes across match moments or dates.

source_card.composition: Archival paper insert over an ink field, with an oversized quote mark and clipped corner.
source_card.visual_encoding: Publication and date precede the highlighted claim; URL sits in its own traceability strip.
source_card.best_for: Giving a claim visible provenance without pretending the source is match footage.
